issues.description: Field/type mismatch for StockIngredient.price and its constructor parameter: The problem statement UML (class StockIngredient) declares price as an int and the constructor signature as StockIngredient(String, int, int) (problem_statement.md lines 42-47). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java lines 5-8) defines price as an int and the constructor accepts an int price. However, the template provided to students (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java lines 5-8) declares the price field and constructor parameter as double (private final double price; public StockIngredient(String name, double price, int quantity) ...) and getPrice() returns double. This inconsistency between the template and the UML/solution will confuse students about the expected price type, may cause subtle compilation/type issues or unnecessary edits when they implement SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery which in the solution use int-priced ingredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across artifacts. Recommended: update the template's StockIngredient to use int for price to match the UML and the solution (change the field to private final int price; constructor parameter to int price; and getPrice() to return int). Alternatively, if fractional prices are intended, update the problem statement and the solution to use double consistently and adjust SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery accordingly. Ensure constructor signatures and getPrice() return types match in all three places (problem statement, template, solution).
